sections.content:
Insightful content of knowing what is international trade, why countries gain from trade, a country's advantages in trade, and a bit of how trade policies impact trade.

I really want it to cover more on the political and policy sides of international trade. But I guess time is not enough.

Before Mid: (Highlight some important topics)
Ricardian model, Heckscher-Ohlin Model, Standard Trade Model.

After Mid:
Economics of Scale
Single Industry analysis (ch9)
Policies: Tariff, Subsidy, Quota
sections.teaching:
Professor Lai is not the best presenter at UST, but I could understand most parts. He sometimes makes too detailed explanations (like making a proof from scratch) of a simple concept for half of the lecture and often time makes students more confused.

But I would say he is a responsive professor, and willing to explain concepts both after class or through email.
sections.grading:
A piece of advice is knowing what are internal and external prices, as they probably cost me 15 points in midterm. (The textbook didn't cover much about it)

Grading: absolute and relative
He said the grade is absolute, but he will adjust with difficulty.

Midterm: avg is around 45. He put way too many questions in the midterm. Even the best students would leave almost a full long question empty (25 points). And the long questions are easier than the MC. (2 long questions, 24 MC with more than 1 answer)

Final: Very similar to the midterm but he adjusts the difficulty. (4 long questions, 36 MC with more than 1 answer)

It's very difficult to get high marks in MC. ~60% is easy with basic understanding and common sense. But above 80% is almost impossible with its deduct policy. So I would prioritize long questions for exam strategy.

Pretty good grading in a 4000 Econ course. (I participate in class, maybe it makes a difference.)
sections.workload:
Nothing too crazy for a 4 credit course.
You could skip reading the textbook (even though it is required)
5 PS, graded by effort.
1 project (presentation+paper)
(He said the quality of the paper is much more important than the presentation. So I guess the presentation is mostly for feedback purposes.)

The only downside is you have to participate in the class and presentation. And it counts quite a lot for the final grade.

sections.content:
The course content is in two parts. (copied from syllabus)
1. Part I discusses the patterns of international trade, why nations trade, what they trade, and who gains from trade, without explicit policy interventions.
2. Part II analyzes the determinants and the implementations of different trade policies, the motives for countries or organizations to restrict or regulate international trade, and the welfare implications of those trade policies.
sections.teaching: Very good professor! One of the best that I've had in UST. She is very passionate and always willing to offer help. She welcomes students to arrange meetings with her to discuss the projects. For our group, she gave us a lot of useful advice and guided us on how to conduct research and do our project. After class, she always stays there for q&a. She also arranged many sessions of career talk by her past students (although I didn't have time for most of the talks...). You can feel that she really cares for her students!
sections.grading:
I think the grading is pretty fair.

sections.workload:
The workload is heavy. She assigned post-lecture assignments every week and gave a limited time to complete. If you do not focus in class, you wouldn't know how to do it.
The group project was fine. She gave us a lot of time to work on it. Only requires more time and effort before handing in the slides and the presentation day. Our group spent quite a lot of time working on the project before the deadline.
For the exams, I spent a lot of time reviewing and watching all the lecture videos. I think the exam itself is not that hard once you understand the concepts and carefully read the questions. The questions can be tricky. All open-book, so it's not that difficult as long as you have everything on your notes.

sections.content: The content is pretty interesting if you are interested in International Trade. The professor always asked thought-provoking questions, such as there is a theory that there will be more trades between two countries if they are having a shorter distance, intuitively the effect should be lower in the modern day with the advanced technology and transportation. However, in reality, the effect is strengthening. She asked 3-4 these kind of questions per lesson, which I find quite interesting. Before Mid term, the content and concept is much harder, you MUST have a good understanding on the correlation between wage, price, labor: capital ratio. It sounds simple but the questions can be really tricky when she added different scenarios. The content after mid term is much easier. Mostly, it focuses on different trade instruments.
sections.teaching: The best professor I have ever meant in HKUST. She poured all her time and resources on this course. I am sure that you can feel her passion and she is willing to spend time to explain any class content or giving you some career advice. Her explanation is clear that I understand most of the content during the class.
sections.grading:
The grading is fair. I got a mean for my midterm while I am 5 marks above the mean for my final and at last I got B+.

sections.content:
The course consists of two major parts. Part 1 is about different trade theories and trade pattern analysis (including quite some graph analysis and calculations which will be heavily tested in the exams). Part 2 is on policy analysis which is more fun and practical. It's a good balance of quantitative analysis and qualitative understandings - will recommend if you're interested in international trade (especially under the current trade war environment).
One of the highlights of the course compared to other ECON courses is that you get to complete a group project of your chosen topic. It provides some hands-on practice of the trade theories and models learned in class and helps you to develop a more in-depth understanding of international trade.
Plus, it's also a good opportunity if you have ECON4670 to fulfill (for ECON-major students)
sections.teaching: Teaching is quite clear. Prof is very experienced and renowned in international trade. She is also a very caring prof, constantly offering her students with guidance on grad school/ job hunting and outside-of-classroom advice.
sections.grading:
70% exams (midterm+final) + 20% group project & presentation + 10% in-class participation.
Overall it's quite hard to get A range even if you have a decent group project and above-mean exam scores (half-SD above). So you should only take this course for its content instead of the grade.
sections.workload: Varies with individual choices because problem sets are optional. But the course material is quite intensive so it requires a fair amount of self-study time. Also, the project requires quite some time in group meetings and meetings with prof.
